title: Islamic Lifting Wisdom
summary: Third in his 'lifting wisdom' series (after Greek and samurai), drawing lessons for lifters from Quran and hadith quotes, applicable even to non-believers. He frames a virtuous cycle of discipline, accepting pain as a gift, combativity, confidence and gratitude, and argues Islam contains a built-in anti-steroid ethic of earning gains legitimately.
claims: Lifters, like religious practitioners, give up drinking, junk food and comfort because they know the sacrifice pays off later
Rejecting instant gratification is a key part of developing yourself as a man
Intoxicants are forbidden in Islam because they breed laxity and self-indulgence, a lesson lifters can apply
Consistency beats intensity: training steadily for a few years is far better than going super hard for two weeks and quitting
Change has three steps: wish it, will it, then get it done, and getting it done requires discipline
Freedom is not the absence of restriction but a chosen set of restrictions you accept because they make you better
What feels good is not necessarily good for you; discipline stands between you and pleasure so you can earn a later reward
Treat pain as a gift rather than a punishment; seeing it as a gift lets you collect the reward it offers
People who avoid hardship and stop competing tend to be the most anxious, depressed and miserable
No challenge you face is truly impossible; pain is an internal sensation, so you alone can defeat it
Discipline is its own reward; pleasure is a petty, base reward
Strong convictions and refusing to back down remove shame, which only slows you down
The best lifters with the best natural physiques he has seen have deep, developed characters
Bodybuilding aims at beauty, a perfection never reached; true beauty comes from discipline, pain and sacrifice, never from indulgence
Gains earned legitimately take longer but last; gains achieved illegitimately (steroids) come faster but cannot be kept
Islam has a built-in anti-steroid stance: it forbids intoxicants and gains obtained illegitimately
Anything you gain naturally you can maintain naturally; shortcuts always cause damage down the line
Confidence is built on past achievements: if you took your arms from 13 to 14 in or your squat from 200 to 300 lb, you can go further
Lifters who start believing their potential is unlimited go far; those who start without faith go nowhere
Faith in your body does not need to be blind: lift for two months and you will grow, and that proof builds the faith
Stop thinking you have bad genetics and keep aiming for more; that mindset produces the best physiques
Be grateful: having two arms, two legs and enough food to grow leaves you no excuse not to try your best
The cycle of discipline, pain, confidence and gratitude never ends; lifters who quit after six months lose all the benefits
Gratitude is the trait that separates wise men from fools
